candidates.attacker_control: A remote, unauthenticated HTTP client controls the Content-Type header. No valid action mapping, authenticated session, or file-upload interceptor is required: the request wrapper is created before action mapping, and the header only needs to contain the substring multipart/form-data.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Confirmed that the default parser is Jakarta, that wrapping happens before action mapping, and that the default message bundle contains only SizeLimitExceededException and IOException upload keys. Checked the configured mitigations: `struts.ognl.allowStaticMethodAccess=false`, `struts.excludedClasses=com.opensymphony.xwork2.ActionContext`, and `struts.excludedPackageNames=java.lang,ognl,javax`. These restrictions may constrain dangerous OGNL operations but do not disable evaluation of the exception-derived default message. Also confirmed that the fileUpload interceptor and a valid action are not needed for this path.
candidates.impact: Server-side evaluation of attacker-controlled OGNL in the request thread, with access to the Struts ValueStack and any reachable application objects. This can disclose or modify application state and can potentially escalate to arbitrary command execution and full server compromise if the configured member-access sandbox can be bypassed. The issue is remotely triggerable without authentication on the default multipart parser configuration.
candidates.prerequisites: The request passes through the Struts filter/servlet path; the default `struts.multipart.parser=jakarta` (or another affected multipart implementation) is active; Commons FileUpload rejects the malformed Content-Type with a message containing the header value; no application-defined localization key for InvalidContentTypeException overrides the fallback; and the resulting expression is not blocked by the configured OGNL member-access restrictions.
candidates.root_cause: JakartaMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage passes FileUploadException.getMessage() as the default localization message. LocalizedTextUtil then applies TextParseUtil.translateVariables to that default message, causing `$`/`%` OGNL expressions to be evaluated on the request ValueStack. Dispatcher.wrapRequest accepts any Content-Type containing multipart/form-data, so a malformed Content-Type reaches Commons FileUpload before action mapping; the FileUpload 1.3.1 rejection message includes the supplied header value and becomes the OGNL-capable message.
candidates.title: Unauthenticated OGNL injection through multipart Content-Type error handling
candidates.trace: StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter creates the ActionContext and calls PrepareOperations.wrapRequest before finding an action. Dispatcher.wrapRequest sees a Content-Type containing multipart/form-data and constructs MultiPartRequestWrapper. JakartaMultiPartRequest.parse calls processUpload/parseRequest; Commons FileUpload throws a FileUploadException for the malformed Content-Type. The catch block calls buildErrorMessage(e), which passes e.getMessage() to LocalizedTextUtil.findText as defaultMessage. The default struts-messages bundle has no InvalidContentTypeException key in the snapshot, so getDefaultMessage falls back to that exception text and calls TextParseUtil.translateVariables. OgnlTextParser extracts `%{...}` or `${...}`, and OgnlValueStack.findValue evaluates it as OGNL before action mapping completes.
candidates.unverified: The exact commons-fileupload 1.3.1 exception text was not verified from the dependency source because that jar is not present in the snapshot, and no runtime request was executed. Full command-execution impact was not demonstrated; the static method/package restrictions could block some sandbox-escape chains. The exact exception class and application-specific localization overrides may vary.
candidates.weakness_type: Expression Language Injection / Remote Code Execution (CWE-917, CWE-94)

coverage_summary: The source scope enumerated 2,648 visible files, and the relation index reports complete coverage of all 2,648 files with no missing/unparsed source files. Inspection focused on the core request pipeline, filters and prepare operations, multipart parsing, localization and OGNL evaluation, security/member-access configuration, default properties and bundles, file-upload handling, action mapping, the REST plugin/XStream handler, static-content loading, and representative showcase actions. The full repository was mapped and searched, but not every peripheral app/plugin file was read line-by-line.
limitations: Commons FileUpload 1.3.1 and other external dependency sources are not present in the snapshot; their runtime exception-message and deserialization behavior was inferred from the imports, versions, and call patterns rather than inspected jar source.
No build, test, scanner, server, or exploit execution was performed; the candidate is a source-grounded lead, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability.
The P1 relation index is syntactic and incomplete for semantic/data-flow resolution; several relevant call edges are unresolved, so reachability was checked manually against source text.

Optional plugins, archetypes, and applications were not exhaustively audited; the selected finding applies to the core default parser configuration, while deployment-specific overrides can change reachability.
A complete sandbox-escape/RCE chain was not validated; the static-method and excluded-package controls may constrain the impact of the injected expression.

rejected_leads.lead: Optional REST plugin XStream deserialization: XStreamHandler.createXStream returns an unconfigured new XStream(), and ContentTypeInterceptor passes the HTTP request body to XStreamHandler.toObject/fromXML.
rejected_leads.reason: This is a serious unhardened deserialization path, but it is only reachable when the optional REST plugin is deployed and an affected action accepts application/xml. It was not selected over the default, pre-action multipart OGNL path; a concrete gadget/type-permission chain was not verified.

rejected_leads.lead: Showcase JSPEvalAction writes the request-supplied `jsp` parameter into /interactive/demo.jsp and then renders it.
rejected_leads.reason: The class is an explicitly interactive showcase/demo artifact and depends on an exploded WAR deployment. It appears intentional for the demo application rather than a framework vulnerability; not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: REST RESTful action mapping can take a method name from the URL path (`action/id/method`).
rejected_leads.reason: The snapshot defaults to strict method invocation with package/global allowed methods, so arbitrary methods are not reachable by default. Not selected without a deployment that disables those restrictions.

summary: Selected one candidate: unauthenticated OGNL injection through the multipart Content-Type/error-message path in the default Struts request pipeline (Struts 2.5-SNAPSHOT). The optional REST XStream deserialization path and a showcase-only JSP evaluator were noted as rejected leads, not additional candidates.
